# PO-S02 notes (stage 1: spike, same branch po-s01)

Workflow: a short single-agent spike with the relaxed rules, to learn what blocks the rest of the migration before the parallel stage. Same measures as PO-S01.
Decisions before the spike: D1 non-null assertions allowed; D2 class index signature allowed; D3 Sequelize models out of scope until the spike shows a type-only pattern; D4 @types for the express family installed by me in commit 7dbc5d92 (package.json +5 lines, package-lock.json +176 lines, 17 packages added, 356 passing afterwards). The agent cannot install anything.
Date: 2026-10-03
Branch: Aung-Min-Myat/po-s01
Prompt: evidence/plans/PO-S02-prompt.md | Context file: CLAUDE.md
Time limit: 45 minutes from the prompt; I stop the agent with Esc.
Allowed interventions: permission prompts (Yes or No) and the standard replies "Yes, that is my instruction. Go." and "Use your judgment." Nothing else.
Progress measure: first-party .ts files outside server/libs excluding .d.ts (14 at start), .js files left (168 at start), build, tests (356), banned tokens, compiled-output changes against the saved baseline copy.

## What happened in the spike (2026-10-03, format ~[HH:MM])

~[04:00] (derived: the first /usage showed a wall time of 3m 55s and the last, read at about 04:55, showed 59m 0s, so the session started at about 03:56) Fresh session, checked with slash commands only: /plugin (Superpowers disabled), /model (Opus 5.5, unchanged), /permissions (20 deny entries, accept edits on) and /usage: Total cost $0.0000, 0 requests, session bar 12%, week 33%, Fable 12% (saved in usage-start.txt). Unlike the PO-S01 run, this session started at zero cost.
~[04:13] I pasted the prompt (evidence/plans/PO-S02-prompt.md) in that session. The time 04:13 is from my own message; the run log header says 04:06, which was only when I wrote the header. Stage base commit d9eea5e9.
~[04:23] (exact, git commit time 04:22:59) b807851a: ScanLogger and EBookFile (target 1). Fields typed T | null with declare; 3 non-null assertions (ScanLogger 1, EBookFile 2), each with a one-line comment. EBookFile takes LibraryFile & { metadata: FileMetadata } as its parameter type, which avoided 4 more assertions.
~[04:28] (exact, git commit time 04:27:57) 188c26ed: Notification and FileMetadata (target 2). A class index signature in each, plus a second index signature on Notification's update-payload interface (my rule only named class index signatures; I accept it as part of the same decision), and 2 assertions on one line in FileMetadata.
~[04:28] My checkpoint (run-log.txt): 18 .ts files, 164 .js files left, 2 commits since d9eea5e9.
~[04:37] (exact, git commit time 04:36:37) 62e24979: ApiCacheManager (target 3). Express types through import type; the response is typed as Omit<Response, 'send'> plus the wrapper and originalSend; Sequelize hook callbacks take object; 1 assertion on Database.sequelize (the agent checked that Database.init runs at Server.js:172, before this init() at :193).
~[04:39] (exact, git commit time 04:39:09) 3dc3e55b: CacheController (target 4). It removed const { Request, Response } = require('express'), which is not type-only: both names are undefined at runtime (the agent checked this) and Server.js loads express first, but the compiled file loses that line.
~[04:49] (agent's clock) Target 5, models/Setting.js, tried from 04:39 to 04:49 and restored with git mv back and git restore; nothing committed. Approaches: A, a straight conversion (6 errors: TS2417 on the class because init(sequelize) does not fit Model.init, TS2684 twice on this.findAll and this.upsert, and TS2345 on the untyped EmailSettings and NotificationSettings constructors). B, adding Model.init's signature as an overload (TS2394 and TS2355). B-prime, an intersection parameter type (clash gone, rejected because the overload would tell callers that init takes attributes and options). C, an uncallable overload static init(this: never, ...args: never[]): never, which removes the clash with no casts. C2 and C3, C plus 2 casts on the two untyped settings constructors, with the overloads placed above the JSDoc: 0 errors, 356 passing, and a compiled file equal to the baseline except for the split sequelize require. The agent believes converting EmailSettings and NotificationSettings first would remove those 2 casts (not checked).
~[04:53] (exact, Claude's footer) The agent ended the run itself after a turn of 25m 42s, under my 45-minute cap (04:58). From my paste at 04:13 that is 40 minutes of wall time, so about 14 minutes (derived) went on my answers to permission prompts.
~[04:55] (derived: the last activity was 1m 51s before the reading) /usage at the end (usage-end.txt): Total cost $4.35 (API-equivalent), API time 14m 11s, wall time 59m 0s, 59 requests, 98% of input tokens from cache. claude-opus-5-5: 720 input, 88.8k output, 7.0m cache read, 146.2k cache write ($4.35); claude-haiku-4-5: 1.2k input, 12 output ($0.0013). Total code changes as Claude Code counts them: 227 lines added, 74 removed (it counts the agent's edits, including the reverted Setting attempts). Plan limits: session 17%, week (all models) 34% (33% at the start), week (Fable) 12%.
~[04:58] (estimate) When I started Claude Code afterwards, it printed a warning for 5 deny rules: Write(test/**), Write(tsconfig.server.json), Write(package.json), Write(package-lock.json) and Write(server/libs/**) are not matched by file permission checks, because only Edit(path) rules are, and Edit rules cover all file-editing tools. So those 5 entries were ignored. The protection stays: the Edit rules for the same paths exist, and my 01:38 test was blocked by Edit(test/**). The PO-S01 notes (01:36) and the settings copy in evidence/context-files list the 5 Write entries as if they were active.
~[04:59] The session ID of the spike (the resume line on exit): 775d6c92-7bcc-43ed-a17b-e497399c44bb.
~[05:00] (estimate) During the run I asked my assistant (this chat) several things: two permission prompts, how to judge prompts in general, the checkpoint log line, why the run had a cap, and whether the budget mattered. I sent the agent no message except the prompt. This chat counts toward the same plan limits as the agent, so the 1-point rise in the weekly bar (33% to 34%) comes from both.

## Result (2026-10-03)

- Stopped at 04:53 (exact, footer) by the agent itself, 40 minutes after my paste (derived). Reason: all five targets were done or reported.
- Files converted: 6 files in 4 commits (ScanLogger, EBookFile, Notification, FileMetadata, ApiCacheManager, CacheController), about 490 lines (raw line counts of the originals from the agent's reads, not the non-blank measure used for PO-S01). First-party .ts files outside server/libs: 20 (was 14). .js files left: 162 (was 168). Of the 182 first-party .js files at the baseline, 20 are now .ts (11.0%). In lines, Phase 1 (805), PO-S01 (896) and this stage (about 490) come to about 2,200 lines, roughly 4.7% of the server (rough, because the measures differ).
- Cost: $4.35 for the spike (the session started at $0.0000), against about $4.88 for the PO-S01 run alone. About $0.009 per raw line against about $0.0054 per non-blank line in PO-S01. The units differ, and the spike includes a 10-minute experiment on Setting.js that produced no committed code, so the per-line figures are rough. Time: about 40 minutes of wall time for about 490 lines is roughly 740 lines per hour, against roughly 1,500 for PO-S01. The spike used about the same output tokens (88.8k against 88.3k) on about half the lines, on harder files.
- My own checks: a clean build from an empty dist-server, three runs: 356 passing each, with no error TS or Debug Failure. git diff against d9eea5e9 for test, tsconfig.server.json, package.json, package-lock.json and server/libs printed nothing; no as any, as unknown as, @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck, @ts-expect-error or ": any" in the .ts files outside server/libs; 0 casts added; 6 non-null assertions and 3 index signatures, each with a one-line comment.
- Compiled output against my copy taken before the spike: 6 files changed, 18 lines added and 14 removed in total (CacheController 1/2, ApiCacheManager 5/4, Notification 3/1, EBookFile 3/3, FileMetadata 1/1, ScanLogger 5/3), no missing files, none over 5 lines.
- One test run during the agent's Setting experiment showed 352 passing and 1 failing; its grep hid the failure text. It did not recur: the agent's 3 later runs and my 3 clean runs all gave 356.
- Possible bugs the agent reported (the prompt named no bug log): AudioFile builds FileMetadata from data.metadata || {}, and the {} fallback leaves every field undefined, so update() never copies anything; nothing in server/ calls ScanLogger.setComplete().
- The agent edited source files with sed -i and node -e, not only with its edit tool. That is inside server/, which is allowed; my deny rules cover file tools only, so a shell write into a protected path would only have been stopped by my answer to the prompt.
- Against my earlier definition: Pass (builds from an empty dist-server, 356 passing, nothing protected changed since the stage base, no banned tokens, no file over 30 changed lines). package.json differs from the PO-S01 base only by my own @types commit (7dbc5d92), made before this stage.
- Not checked: the server was never started; any types that come from untyped JavaScript are not counted; I did not record how many prompts I answered Yes and No.

content.text:
All three models are converted and committed, each with a passing build and 356 passing tests. The uncallable overload does the job, but CLAUDE.md's description of it needs two corrections and one addition.

## Per model

| Model | Converted | Commit | `!` | Index signatures | Casts | Compiled file vs your baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Setting | yes | 3f3963d2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | +5 / −4 lines, all `require` lines |
| LibraryFolder | yes | 3f6a5fd8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | +2 / −1, the `require` line |
| Session | yes | 96f5fc41 | 0 | 0 | 0 | +2 / −1, the `require` line |

Nothing was restored, so there are no compiler errors for an unconverted file. `server/types/` was not needed, and no file outside the three models changed. Across the whole `dist-server`, only these three compiled files differ from the baseline.

The `init` shape is identical in all three:

```ts
  static init(this: never, ...args: never[]): never // uncallable: keeps the static side assignable to Model.init, which this method replaces
  static init(sequelize: Sequelize): void
  /**
   * Initialize model
   * @param {import('../Database').sequelize} sequelize
   */
  static init(sequelize: Sequelize): void {
```

## Did the pattern work as written?

The overload line itself works exactly as written: it removes TS2417 with no cast, including for `hasMany`, `belongsTo`, `create`, `destroy` and `upsert`. Three things around it had to change:

1. **The JSDoc placement in CLAUDE.md is reversed.** I built `Setting` with the JSDoc above the overloads first, and the compiled file lost the 4-line `init` comment. The overloads must go above the JSDoc so the comment stays on the implementation. The PO-S02 notes have it the right way round.
2. **The real signature must be repeated as a second overload.** Read literally (one uncallable overload directly above the method), the implementation signature is hidden and a TypeScript caller gets `TS2684: The 'this' context of type 'typeof X' is not assignable to method's 'this' of type 'never'`. The build hides this today because `Database.js` is unchecked JavaScript.
3. **The constructor parameters must be optional**, which CLAUDE.md does not mention. I used `constructor(values?: CreationAttributes<X>, options?: BuildOptions)`. With required parameters, `this.findAll()` fails with `TS2684 … Type 'typeof X' is not assignable to type 'new () => X'`.

Points 2 and 3 come from scratch probes outside the repo, not from the build. The import shape used in all three is:

```ts
import sequelizeModule = require('sequelize')
const { DataTypes, Model } = sequelizeModule
import type { BuildOptions, CreationAttributes, Sequelize } from 'sequelize'
```

## Judgment calls you may want to overrule

- **`Setting.value`** (JSDoc: `Object`) is a union of the three stored settings shapes, each with a literal `id`. This lets `find((se) => se.id === 'email-settings')` narrow on its own, so the boundary cast the PO-S03 commit predicted was not needed. It relies on TypeScript 5.5 or later (5.9.3 is installed).
- **Session field types** differ from the constructor JSDoc in three places:
  - `lastRefreshToken` and `lastRefreshTokenExpiresAt` allow `null`, because `init()` sets `allowNull: true`.
  - `refreshToken` is declared although the constructor does not list it.
- **The alias is `sequelizeModule`**, so the `sequelize` parameter of `init` does not shadow it (same idea as `axiosModule`).
- **The Setting commit shows as delete + add** in git. Similarity is 42%, under git's 50% default, because a 1.6 KB file gained 1.3 KB of types. `git mv` was used, and `git show -M40%` shows the rename.

## Findings

The prompt named no bug log and limited edits to the three files, so these are only here:

- **Session JSDoc:** it names `import('./User').User`, which does not exist; `User.js` exports the class itself.
- **`createSession` inputs:** `TokenManager.js` passes `getClientIp(req)` (can return null) and `req.headers['user-agent']` (can be undefined). Both columns are nullable, so nothing fails at runtime. I typed the parameters `string`, as the field JSDoc says, so expect two errors there when TokenManager is converted. Widen the types then instead of asserting.

## Not checked

- The server was never started.
- I did not build from an empty `dist-server`; the non-incremental no-emit check passed after each model.
- Counts: first-party `.ts` went from 41 to 44. In-scope `.js` went down by 3; I count 125 → 122 with your exclusions, against your 126 at the start, so our counting differs by one file.

The three test outputs and the three probe files are in the session scratchpad, if you want them for `evidence/test-results/PO-S04/`:
`C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--SEM-2-574-Project-audiobookshelf-po\2d937ae2-1250-4078-888b-80d673301105\scratchpad`

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Why zero casts was possible:** Sequelize's `ModelStatic<M>` is `NonConstructor<typeof Model> & { new(): M }`. That is exactly two requirements — a static side assignable to `Model`'s, and a constructor callable with no arguments. The overload satisfies the first and the optional constructor parameters the second, which is why every association and query call then type-checks untouched.
- **Unchecked JavaScript callers hide type holes.** Finding 2 was invisible to the build because the only caller of `init` is `Database.js`. In a leaf-first migration, checking a converted file from a TypeScript caller's point of view catches what the build cannot yet see.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
